newsitem.title: NORWAY: FOCUS - Non-core operations fuel DnB profit.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Non-core operations fuel DnB profit.

text.p: Den norske Bank (DnB), Norway's largest bank, on Tuesday said first-quarter net profit rose 54 million crowns to 820 million ($115.6 million), mainly boosted by a 27 percent rise from operations outside its core banking activities.

DnB said it saw healthy gains in profits from trading in foreign exchange and financial instruments and brisk stock market activity resulted in high commission income from securities trading and custodial services.

Operating income from other operations amounted to 856 million crowns, up from 673 million in the three-month period a year ago, including net profits of 67 million from insurance arm Vital Forsikring.

Meanwhile, the group's core business booked net interest income of 1.06 billion crowns in the first quarter, largely stable versus last year's 1.07 billion crowns, as higher volumes offset the effect of a continuing squeeze on lending and deposit margins.
Group operating expenses for the three-month period were steady at 1.13 billion crowns.
"There is sound growth within all business areas and measures to cut costs by boosting efficiency are being pursued," Finn Hvistendahl, group managing director, said in a statement.

"We have also succeeded in bringing down credit risk and reducing loan losses significantly. I expect steady growth in DnB's operations in the months ahead, while conditions appear favourable for a continued low level of loan losses."
First-quarter income included net reversals on loan losses and guarantees of 43 million crowns. Earnings per share were booked at 1.28 crowns.
The results were above market expectations and DnB's share price rose three percent to 26.40 crowns in brisk early trade before settling back around 25.80.

Hvistendahl said the bank, which is currently in a bidding war to take over niche mortgage lender Bolig og Naeringsbanken (BNbank), remained committed to providing services across the entire financial market.

"Our bid to acquire BNbank is part of this effort. BNbank will strengthen the DnB group's position in the market for long-term mortgage loans while doubling its market share in the Troendelag region," he said.
The bank's insurance arm, Vital, posted gains in the first quarter with profits for allocation to policyholders, equity and taxes almost doubling to 597 million crowns from 313 million.

DnB said sales of insurance policies through the bank had risen with 63 percent of Vital's overall sales of individual life insurance policies so far this year being channelled through the bank's branch network.

It said the group's tax charge for the period was calculated at six million crowns, based on the bank maintaining its position concerning two disputes with Norwegian tax authorities and on the probability of a solution in DnB's favour.
